Mr. Nikhilesh Dutta, D.A.G. ------ for the opposite party.
parties:
Shamim alias Kazi Shamim
Vs.
The State
full_judgment:
Khademul Islam Chowdhury, J: Accused Kazi Shamim obtained this rule to seek bail in G.R. Case No.148 of 1999 arising out of Balagonj P.S.Case No.15 dated 19.6.1999 under sections 147/148/149/ 129/324/ 307/380/ 427/ 114 of the Penal Code now pending for trial in the court of the Additional District Magistrate, Sylhet. 

 2. The prosecution case in short, is that, one Raja Mia, son of Moyna Mia as informant lodged a First Information Report with Balagonj P.S. on 19.6.1999 alleging that on 19.6.1999 at about 10.11 a.m. while accused Shahid was taking away soil from grave yard to his house and accused Mokbul, was taking away soil to a road and he protested F.I.R. named accused Nos. 1-4 taking some miscreants of the village with them conspired and attacked his house and started throwing stones and cut away trees. When his brother Atique Mia came out from his house the accused Shamim and Nazrul fired gun shots causing grievous bleeding injuries and victim fell down on the ground. Furthermore the accused persons took away valuable goods and money from their house. The accused petitioner and two others surrendered before the High Court Division with prayer for anticipatory bail in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.47 of 2000. The High Court Division upon hearing directed the petitioner to surrender before the court concerned with a direction to the law enforces not to arrest or harass the accused within 3(three) weeks. Accordingly the petitioner surrendered before the court of the learned Additional District Magistrate and were enlarged on bail. After investigation police submitted Charge Sheet in the case vide Charge Sheet No.152 dated 8.9.1999 against petitioner and others under section 147/148/ 149/448/297/ 324/ 307/ 380/ 326/ 427/ 114 of the Penal Code. The informant of the case filed a Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 6349 of 2001 before the High Court Division with the allegation of practising forgery and tempering the F.I.R. annexed to the petition. After hearing the High Court Division cancelled the bail of three accused persons including the accused petitioner and directed to initiate proceedings against person/persons connected with forgery of the contents of the F.I.R. Thereafter Mr. Ranjit Kumar Das, Magistrate, 1st Class filed petition Case No.39 of 2003 against the accused petitioner on the basis of order of the Additional District Magistrate, Sylhet for committing forgery in respect of Judicial record and sent the petition to Kotwali P.S. for necessary action. The accused petitioner was arrested by the Police on 11.2.2004. The learned Session Judge Sylhet on hearing both the parties rejected the prayer for bail of the accused petitioner by order dated 7.6.2004. Against order of refusal of bail by the learned Sessions Judge the accused petitioner moved this court and obtained the Rule. 

 3. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned advocate appearing for the accused petitioner submits that though High Court Division cancel the bail and directed to initiate appropriate proceeding against the accused petitioners and a separate case being Balagonj Petition Case No.39 of 2003 has been started against the accused petitioner under Sections 193/196/ 199/200/463/471 of the Penal Code who was arrested and the case is still pending. But pendency of such a case itself does not prima-facie prove that the accused petitioner committed the offence which is a matter of trial and in view of the fact that the accused petitioner has been granted bail in that case by the trial court the Sessions Judge should have considered the prayer for bail of the accused petitioner. There is no rule that only because the High Court Division cancelled bail the accused can not be admitted to fresh bail. 

 4. The learned Deputy Attorney General vehemently opposes the prayer for bail. According to him the accused petitioner obtained order for surrender with direction upon the law enforcing agency by committing a gigantic fraud by changing a material fact in the F.I.R. and as such he is not entitled to get bail in this case. 

 5. Perused the F.I.R. Charge Sheet and the order of cancellation of bail dated 5.11.2002 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 6349 of 2001 and the impugned order. 

 6. It appear that in canceling bail of the accused petitioner and others in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.6349 of 2001 the High Court Division held that the accused petitioner and others obtained an order of surrender in the Court below from the High Court Division by way mispresentation of the F.I.R. swearing affidavit and changing the false overt act so done by them. 

 7. Bail is granted to a person accused of non bailable offence entirely at the discretion of the court having regard to facts and circumstances of each case and provision of law laid down in section 497 Sub-section (1) (2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The con-current power given to the High Court Division or Sessions Judge to admit any person to bail under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure by recording in writing his or its reason for so doing is absolutely unfettered and High Court Division or Court of Sessions in exercise of discretion may also re-consider prayer for bail after rejection or cancellation of bail. But in view of the provision to re-arrest or commit any person to custody as provided under section 497(5) of the Code of Criminal Procedure where High Court Division cancels bail granted by the Subordinate Court and passed order of re-arrest of any accused bail of such person can not be considered by the Sessions Judge. In the instant case bail granted to the accused petitioner by the learned Additional District Magistrate has been cancelled on the prayer of the informant by the High Court Division. It appears that after cancellation of bail by the High Court Division accused petitioner approached the learned Sessions Judge for bail contending that he has no knowledge as to the tempering in the F.I.R. and he is in jail since 12.2.2004 and that police failed to collect any tangible material against him. The learned Sessions Judge, rejected the bail prayer holding inter alia, that the informant preferred Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.6349 of 2001 alleging that petitioner and two others obtained the order of surrender by suppressing real fact with oblique motive that F.I.R. which was filed by the accused in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 4716 of 2000 was tempered and forged one; the fact of cancellation of bail by the High Court Division on the facts and circumstances of the case is also admitted and as such the accused petitioner is not entitled to get release in the form of bail. 

 10. The Judgment dated 9.11.2002 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 6349 of 2001 filed by the learned advocate for the accused petitioner at the time of hearing be kept with the record.
